record_metadata.category: Internet infrastructure / naming system / application-layer protocol
record_metadata.source_basis: User-provided Domain Name System reference article
record_metadata.primary_purpose: Resolve human-readable domain names into machine-readable network resource information, most prominently IP addresses

core_concept.simple_explanation: DNS provides the naming layer that allows humans and applications to refer to network resources using names instead of remembering numerical network addresses.
core_concept.important_qualification: DNS is more sophisticated than a simple phone book because the same domain name can resolve differently for different users, locations, networks, or circumstances.
core_concept.architectural_goal: Avoid maintaining one enormous centralized host table by distributing authority throughout a hierarchical namespace.

primary_operation.name: forward_name_resolution
primary_operation.description: Translate a domain name into one or more resource records, commonly IP addresses.

other_operations.description: Translate an IP address into a domain name using PTR records.
Identify mail exchangers responsible for receiving mail for a domain.
Represent an alias from one DNS name to another.
Identify authoritative name servers for a zone.
Publish DNSSEC and related security records.
Publish arbitrary textual data used by numerous applications and policies.

internet_naming_model.dns_role: DNS provides translation and association between domain names and Internet resource information.

important_distinction.routing: Mechanism that determines how packets reach IP destinations

logical_flow: Local resolver determines whether the answer is already available
Cached answer is returned if valid
Otherwise the resolver performs upstream DNS resolution
Root hierarchy may identify the relevant TLD servers
TLD servers identify authoritative servers for the requested domain
Authoritative server returns the requested resource record
Recursive resolver caches the result according to TTL
Resolver returns the result to the client
Application uses the returned resource information to contact the destination

top_level_domain.description: Rightmost meaningful label in an ordinary domain name

hostname_or_service_name.description: Specific DNS name used to identify a host or service

tree_properties.label: Individual component between dots
tree_properties.resource_records: Data associated with a DNS name
tree_properties.delegation: Transfer of authority for a subtree

labels.definition: Individual components of a domain name

hostname_preferred_character_set.hyphen_restriction: Labels may not start or end with a hyphen

internationalized_domain_names.problem: Traditional DNS hostname syntax is based around a restricted ASCII representation.
internationalized_domain_names.application_role: Applications such as browsers convert user-facing Unicode domain names into DNS-compatible representations.
internationalized_domain_names.security_consideration: Internationalized names can create visually confusable strings and contribute to homograph phishing attacks.

zones.definition: Administrative portion of the DNS namespace managed by an authority.
zones.relationship_to_tree: A zone represents a portion of the DNS tree beginning at some node.
zones.zone_authority: A designated set of authoritative name servers

delegation.purpose: Transfer authority over a subtree to another administrative entity
delegation.mechanism: Parent zone publishes NS records identifying child authoritative servers

zone_file.purpose: Conventional structured representation of DNS resource records

delegation.definition: Mechanism by which responsibility for a portion of the DNS namespace is assigned to another set of name servers.
delegation.child_role: Provides authoritative information for the delegated zone.
delegation.glue_required_when: Authoritative name server hostname is itself located inside the delegated domain.
delegation.glue_function: Provides the IP address needed to reach the child name server and breaks the circular dependency.

root_name_servers.function: Direct resolvers toward authoritative servers for TLDs
root_name_servers.direct_answer_behavior: Normally provide referrals rather than final answers for ordinary domain records
root_name_servers.global_distribution: Root service is distributed globally, including via anycast instances.

tld_name_servers.function: Direct resolvers toward authoritative servers for delegated domains beneath the TLD

authoritative_name_server.role: Definitive source for DNS records within a zone
authoritative_name_server.data_source: Configured zone data or authorized dynamic updates

primary_authoritative_server.function: Source for authoritative data and zone synchronization

secondary_authoritative_server.role: Maintains a synchronized copy of authoritative zone data

recursive_resolver.role: Performs DNS resolution on behalf of clients

stub_resolver.function: Typically sends queries to a configured recursive resolver

forwarder.description: DNS server that forwards queries to another resolver instead of performing full recursion itself.

authoritative_dns.definition: DNS service that answers from authoritative zone data rather than merely returning cached information.

required_redundancy.concept: Multiple authoritative servers are normally deployed

lame_delegation.description: A delegation points toward a server that does not actually provide authoritative data for the delegated zone.

dns_resolution.overview: DNS resolution converts a requested domain name into resource-record information.

normal_recursive_resolution.step_1: Application requests resolution of a domain name.
normal_recursive_resolution.step_3: If no usable cached result exists, the resolver sends a query to its recursive DNS server.
normal_recursive_resolution.step_4: Recursive resolver checks its own cache.
normal_recursive_resolution.step_5: If necessary, recursive resolver queries a root server.
normal_recursive_resolution.step_6: Root server returns a referral toward the appropriate TLD servers.
normal_recursive_resolution.step_7: Recursive resolver queries a TLD server.
normal_recursive_resolution.step_8: TLD server returns a referral toward authoritative name servers for the requested domain.
normal_recursive_resolution.step_9: Recursive resolver queries an authoritative name server.
normal_recursive_resolution.step_10: Authoritative server returns the requested record.
normal_recursive_resolution.step_11: Recursive resolver caches the result according to applicable TTL rules.
normal_recursive_resolution.step_12: Recursive resolver returns the result to the client.
normal_recursive_resolution.step_13: Application uses the resulting IP address or other resource information.

important.reason: Caching means recursive resolvers frequently already possess the necessary delegation or answer.
important.result: Only a relatively small fraction of DNS requests need to reach root infrastructure.

recursive_query.meaning: Requester asks a DNS server to obtain the complete answer.
recursive_query.behavior: Server performs additional DNS queries as necessary.

iterative_query.meaning: DNS server provides the best information it currently has, potentially including a referral to another server.
iterative_query.typical_use: Recursive resolver communicating with root, TLD, and authoritative infrastructure.

non_recursive_query.meaning: Server responds using data already available to it without performing recursion on behalf of the requester.

dns_cache.purpose: Temporarily store DNS results to avoid repeatedly traversing the hierarchy.

ttl.name: Time To Live
ttl.purpose: Determines how long a cached DNS record can normally remain valid.
ttl.effect: Lower TTL generally allows changes to be observed sooner but increases query traffic.
ttl.high_ttl_effect: Reduces query traffic but can cause old records to remain cached longer.

negative_caching.purpose: Cache information that a requested record or name does not exist.
negative_caching.result: Reduces repeated queries for nonexistent names.

propagation_model.important_concept: DNS changes are not necessarily visible everywhere immediately.
propagation_model.reason: Existing cached responses remain valid until their TTL expires or are otherwise refreshed.
propagation_model.operational_implication: Changing DNS records can produce a transition period where different resolvers have different answers.

resource_records.definition: Structured pieces of information associated with DNS names.

general_fields.NAME: DNS name to which the record applies

A.purpose: Maps a name to an IPv4 address

AAAA.purpose: Maps a name to an IPv6 address

CNAME.purpose: Alias from one DNS name to another canonical DNS name

MX.purpose: Specifies mail exchangers for a domain

NS.purpose: Identifies authoritative name servers for a zone

SOA.purpose: Start of Authority information for a zone

SRV.purpose: Service discovery and service endpoint information

resource_record_set.definition: Set of records of the same name and type
resource_record_set.ordering: DNS does not inherently require a special ordering of records within an RRset
resource_record_set.possible_load_distribution: Servers may vary response ordering, including round-robin techniques.

reverse_dns.purpose: Resolve an IP address back to a domain name.
reverse_dns.important_property: Multiple names may be associated with a single IP address, so reverse DNS does not necessarily provide a unique identity for an IP.

glue_records.problem: A delegated zone can name an authoritative server whose own hostname exists inside the delegated zone.

circular_dependency.problem: Resolving example.org requires finding ns1.example.org, but ns1.example.org itself is inside example.org.

glue_records.purpose: Provide the IP address of the child authoritative name server so resolution can proceed.

transaction_id.purpose: Associate a response with a query

properties: Used when DNS transport requirements call for TCP

dns_over_tls.primary_goal: Encrypt DNS traffic between client and resolver/server

dns_over_https.important_property: DNS traffic is transported using the HTTPS protocol stack.

dns_over_quic.design_goal: Provide DNS privacy properties associated with encrypted transport while retaining latency characteristics associated with modern connectionless DNS transport.

dnscrypt.description: Non-IETF protocol for encrypted DNS communication
dnscrypt.historical_role: Provided encrypted DNS transport and influenced privacy-oriented DNS deployment.

privacy.privacy_problem: Traditional DNS was designed primarily for distributed naming and caching rather than confidentiality.
potential_observers: Other parties able to observe DNS traffic

privacy_technologies.ODoH: Separates knowledge of client identity from knowledge of the requested name through proxying architecture.
privacy_technologies.VPN: Moves DNS resolution into or through the VPN's network path.
privacy_technologies.Tor: Can route DNS-related activity through anonymity infrastructure.

encrypted_dns: Changes who can observe DNS queries
Can complicate enterprise DNS policy enforcement
Can shift resolver concentration toward large public providers

original_design.security_priority: Limited in the original DNS design
original_design.historical_context: DNS originated in an environment that was substantially different from today's public commercial Internet.

cache_poisoning.description: False DNS data is inserted into a resolver cache so subsequent clients receive incorrect answers.

dns_spoofing.description: Forged or misleading DNS responses are presented as legitimate.

dns_hijacking.description: DNS resolution behavior is redirected or altered by an unauthorized party or system.

man_in_the_middle.description: An intermediary interferes with DNS communication.
man_in_the_middle.risk: Manipulation or observation of DNS queries and responses.

dns_leak.description: DNS queries escape an intended privacy tunnel or security boundary.
dns_leak.example: A VPN is active but DNS requests are still sent to an external resolver outside the VPN path.

domain_hijacking.description: Unauthorized control over a registered domain or its management infrastructure.

idn_homograph_attack.description: Visually similar Unicode characters are used to create deceptive domain names.
idn_homograph_attack.security_effect: Users may mistake a malicious domain for a legitimate one.

dns_covert_channel.description: DNS traffic is abused to transport commands or data unrelated to ordinary name resolution.

dnssec.purpose: Provide cryptographic authentication of DNS data.
dnssec.problem_addressed: Traditional DNS responses do not inherently provide cryptographic proof that returned DNS data originated from the correct DNS authority.
dnssec.important_distinction: DNSSEC authenticates DNS data; it is not the same thing as encrypting DNS traffic.

edns.purpose: Extend DNS protocol capabilities without redesigning the basic DNS message format.
capabilities: Larger DNS message sizes over UDP

dynamic_dns.purpose: Dynamically update DNS records as network addresses change.

zone_transfers.purpose: Synchronize DNS zone data between authoritative servers.

security.related: TSIG and other authentication mechanisms can be used to authenticate trusted DNS operations.

multi_ip_resolution.description: One hostname may resolve to multiple IP addresses.

multi_hostname_single_ip.description: Multiple hostnames may resolve to the same IP address.

cdn_integration.description: DNS can direct different users toward different service endpoints.
cdn_integration.mechanism: Different DNS responses can be returned depending on resolver context, geography, network, policy, or service architecture.

anycast_relationship.concept: The same IP address can be announced from multiple network locations.
anycast_relationship.dns_role: DNS can return an anycast address, after which Internet routing determines the network location reached.

basic_flow: DNS resolver asks for the domain's address
DNS infrastructure determines an appropriate service endpoint
DNS returns one or more addresses
Client connects to the selected endpoint
CDN or edge infrastructure serves the content
why_dns_matters: DNS can distribute clients among service locations
DNS allows services to change infrastructure without changing user-facing names
DNS enables geographically distributed service architectures
dns_and_cdn_architecture.important_limitation: DNS does not itself transport the application data; it supplies the information needed for the application to locate the service.

registrant.definition: Person or organization requesting use of a domain name.

registrar.definition: Organization authorized to register domain names within applicable registry systems.

registry.definition: Operator responsible for the authoritative database for a domain namespace, particularly a TLD.

tld_operator.role: Administrative and technical operation of a top-level domain.

relationship: Registry maintains the authoritative registration database
DNS delegation identifies authoritative name servers
Authoritative DNS servers publish operational records

registration_vs_dns.registration: Establishes administrative control/use of a domain name.
registration_vs_dns.dns: Publishes resource records that make the domain operational on the network.

complete_dns_lookup_example.scenario: Client has no usable cached answer.

step_01_application.action: Requests the IP address associated with www.example.com.

step_02_stub_resolver.action: Checks local DNS information and configured resolver.

step_04_root.root_response: Referral toward the authoritative infrastructure for .com.

step_05_tld.response: Referral toward authoritative name servers for example.com.

step_09_application_connection.action: Uses returned IP address to initiate the actual network connection.

critical_distinction.http: Carries web application requests and responses.

nx_domain.meaning: Requested domain name does not exist according to the responding DNS authority.

servfail.meaning: Resolver/server was unable to successfully complete the requested operation.

timeout.meaning: Expected DNS response does not arrive within the applicable timeout.

lame_delegation.meaning: Delegated server does not provide the expected authoritative information.

stale_cache.meaning: Client or intermediary continues using old information due to caching behavior.

arpanet_predecessor.maintainer: Stanford Research Institute Network Information Center
arpanet_predecessor.problem: Manual centralized maintenance became increasingly difficult as the network expanded.

elizabeth_feinler.role: Developed and maintained the early ARPANET directory

jon_postel.role: Maintained numerical addressing coordination and helped direct the effort that resulted in DNS.

paul_mockapetris.motivation: Replace the increasingly unwieldy centralized host table with an automated hierarchical naming architecture.

updated_specifications.significance: These became the foundational DNS specifications.

isc.role: Home for BIND development and maintenance

Elizabeth_Feinler.role: Early ARPANET directory and host naming administration

Jon_Postel.role: Internet addressing coordination and DNS development leadership context

SRI.role: Early ARPANET host naming and directory administration

IETF.role: Publishes DNS protocol specifications and extensions through RFCs

ICANN.role: Internet domain-name and numbering coordination ecosystem

TLD_registries.role: Operate authoritative registration databases for TLD namespaces

registrars.role: Provide domain registration services to registrants

dns_in_the_modern_internet.role: Naming control plane for Internet applications

importance.human_usability: Users can access services through memorable names rather than numerical addresses.
importance.infrastructure_flexibility: Service IP addresses can change without requiring users to learn a new domain.
importance.distribution: Different DNS answers can support globally distributed service architectures.
importance.fault_tolerance: Multiple DNS records and servers can provide redundancy.

dns.purpose: Associates domain names with IP addresses and other DNS resource information.

routing.purpose: Determines how IP packets are forwarded through networks.

complete_web_request_model.key_insight: DNS is normally one of the first network services involved in locating an Internet application, but DNS itself does not carry the application's content.

wildcards.purpose: Generate matching DNS records for otherwise unspecified names within a zone.

query_name_minimization.purpose: Reduce unnecessary disclosure of the full requested domain name during iterative resolution.

split_horizon_dns.purpose: Return different DNS answers depending on which client/network is querying.

multicast_dns.purpose: Local-network name resolution without requiring conventional unicast DNS infrastructure.
multicast_dns.relationship: Related technology influenced by the DNS naming model.

dns_control_plane.purpose: Determines where applications should attempt to connect.

control_plane_model.important_concept: DNS can influence where traffic goes without being the mechanism that actually transports that traffic.

mental_model.simple: Name -> DNS -> IP/resource information -> routing -> connection -> application
expanded: Recursive resolver performs hierarchy traversal if needed

dns_is_not: A database in the ordinary centralized sense
A guarantee that an IP address represents a unique physical machine

modern_distributed_dns.role: Global service discovery, CDNs, cloud infrastructure, enterprise networking, and Internet applications

primary_protocol_references.title: Domain Names - Implementation and Specification
primary_protocol_references.role: DNS protocol implementation and wire format

primary_protocol_references.title: Dynamic Updates in the Domain Name System

source_caveats.scope: This schema follows the supplied DNS article as the primary source and organizes its technical material into a machine-readable architecture.
source_caveats.historical_material: Historical claims are represented according to the supplied source rather than independently reconciled.
source_caveats.protocol_evolution: DNS has accumulated many extensions beyond the original 1983 protocol.
source_caveats.transport_distinction: Traditional DNS commonly uses UDP/TCP port 53, while newer privacy transports such as DoT, DoH, DoQ, and DoC use different protocol stacks.
source_caveats.dns_vs_registration: Domain registration and DNS operation are related but distinct systems.
source_caveats.dns_vs_routing: DNS provides naming/resource information; IP routing determines how packets reach an IP destination.
source_caveats.caching: DNS answers can differ temporarily across resolvers because of caching and TTL behavior.
source_caveats.security: DNSSEC provides authentication/integrity for DNS data but should not be confused with encryption of DNS traffic.

record_integrity.schema_goal: Represent DNS as an end-to-end Internet naming and resolution system.
record_integrity.conceptual_pipeline: Domain Name -> Resolver -> Cache/Hierarchy -> Authoritative DNS -> Resource Record -> IP/Service Endpoint -> Internet Routing -> Application Connection
